modes.label: Interactive CodeBuild Sandbox Linux GPU
modes.note: us-east-1 price list: Sandbox-Sec:LinuxGPU g1.small $0.00032/s, g1.large $0.00181/s. AWS does not name the GPU model, so this mode has no gpu map and is gated behind opt-in (alt). Price-list metadata lists g1.large as 48 vCPU / 192 GiB; docs say 32 vCPU / 255 GiB. Default Linux GPU concurrency quota is 0.

modes.label: On-demand EC2 Linux GPU
modes.note: us-east-1: gpu1.small $0.05/min, gpu1.large $0.30/min. The GPU model is not named in the AWS compute table, so there is no gpu map and the mode is opt-in (alt). Default concurrency quota is 0 for Linux GPU.

modes.label: Reserved fleet Linux GPU
modes.commit_note: Reserved-capacity fleet: each instance is billed from request until termination (60-minute minimum), and a fleet keeps at least its base capacity provisioned, so it is priced as always-on. AWS does not name the GPU models. Non-monotonic prices reflect different underlying instance families.

modes.label: On-demand Lambda Arm
modes.note: us-east-1 list rates ($0.00001/s for 1GB, scaling with memory). AWS publishes memory only; vCPU follows Lambda's memory-proportional allocation (about 1 vCPU per 1.77 GB, max 6), rounded down. Lambda compute limits: no root, no Docker builds or runs, writes only to /tmp, no caching, no VPC, no SSH, and runs capped at 15 minutes. Available in 10 regions.

modes.label: On-demand Lambda x86-64
modes.note: us-east-1 list rates ($0.00002/s for 1GB, scaling with memory). AWS publishes memory only; vCPU follows Lambda's memory-proportional allocation, rounded down. Lambda compute limits: no root, no Docker, writes only to /tmp, no caching, no VPC, no SSH, and runs capped at 15 minutes.

modes.label: Interactive CodeBuild Sandbox Linux x86-64
modes.note: Interactive debug sandbox; us-east-1 list rates. Price varies by region.

modes.label: Interactive CodeBuild Sandbox Arm
modes.note: Interactive debug sandbox; us-east-1 list rates.

modes.label: Interactive CodeBuild Sandbox Windows
modes.note: Interactive debug sandbox; us-east-1 list rates.

modes.label: Reserved fleet Linux x86-64
modes.commit_note: Billed from the request for a fleet instance until its termination, not only while a build runs; 60-minute minimum per instance. A fleet keeps its base capacity provisioned, so it is priced as always-on. Many custom EC2 instance-type and NVMe SKUs also exist.

modes.label: Reserved fleet macOS Arm M2
modes.commit_note: Reserved-capacity fleet: each Mac instance has a 24-hour minimum before release and bills while provisioned, so it is priced as always-on. us-east-1 list prices.

modes.label: Reserved fleet Linux Arm
modes.commit_note: Billed from the fleet-instance request until termination; 60-minute minimum; the fleet keeps base capacity provisioned, so it is priced as always-on. us-east-1 attribute-based list rates.

modes.label: Reserved fleet Windows
modes.commit_note: Only attribute sizes with explicit us-east-1 catalog rows are listed. Billed until fleet-instance termination, minimum 60 minutes; the fleet keeps base capacity provisioned, so it is priced as always-on.

plans.name: Pay as you go
plans.note: Free tier: 100 build minutes/month on general1.small or arm1.small = $0.50 (encoded on general1.small). Build timeout max 36 h (CodeBuild quota, not verified today).

perf_source: No benchmark row: provider is not in ComputeSDK results or the HPC run (as of 2026-09-28). See research/perf-map.json.
caveats: Lambda compute (per-second, 1-10 GB) and reserved-capacity fleets not encoded.
Prices are us-east-1; other regions differ.
CloudWatch Logs, S3 artifacts and data transfer billed separately.
EC2 on-demand builds run in containers on CodeBuild-managed hosts (LINUX_CONTAINER) or EC2 (LINUX_EC2).
Free tier also includes 6,000 Lambda build-seconds/month on lambda.arm.1GB or lambda.x86-64.1GB (about $0.06-$0.12); not encoded, and it does not cover Sandbox, reserved or Docker image server usage.

fleet.tiers: Per region and per compute type. Current table shows 1 for most listed sizes, 0 for Linux GPU Small/Large and Linux 2XLarge, while a note says some platforms/types default to 20 and internal metrics determine defaults. Reserved compute fleets: maximum 10 fleets; running-instance defaults mostly 1 and 0 for 2XLarge/GPU.
fleet.notes: New builds queue at account/type quota; queue capacity is five times the concurrent limit. Treat 1 only as the table default for the common listed type, not a universal account cap.

extras.price: us-east-1 per second: Linux x86 small $0.00003, medium $0.00006, large $0.00012, xlarge $0.0005, 2xlarge $0.001; Arm small $0.00003, medium $0.00006, large $0.00012, xlarge $0.00047, 2xlarge $0.00094. Stays active for up to a 1-hour cooldown after the last image build, then a lower cache-at-rest charge applies until the feature is disabled.

snapshot_auto.note: Each build/sandbox is a fresh ephemeral environment; nothing is checkpointed on stop or timeout (sandbox sample shows RUNNING_SANDBOX TIMED_OUT then STOPPED). Only build caches (S3 cache, local source/Docker-layer/custom cache) and the paid Docker image server carry data between builds - not machine-state snapshots.

snapshot_on_demand.note: The full CodeBuild API operation list has no snapshot/checkpoint/image-capture action (only Start/Stop Build, Start/Stop Sandbox, StartCommandExecution, InvalidateProjectCache, fleets etc.). Reserved fleets can boot from a custom AMI, but that is not a snapshot of a running build.

harness_api.note: CodeBuild sandbox offers StartSandbox / StartCommandExecution / SSH via SSM (generic exec), no API to drive an agent harness.

egress_allowlist.quote: Denies outgoing traffic to all destinations by default.
egress_allowlist.note: Managed proxy for reserved-capacity fleets: defaultBehavior ALLOW_ALL/DENY_ALL plus orderedProxyRules of type DOMAIN or IP with ALLOW/DENY (max 100, API_FleetProxyRule). 'not supported for VPC, Windows, or MacOS'; extra charge while configured; CodeBuild sets HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY. For on-demand builds, egress control is via VPC config (subnets + security-group egress rules, NAT, or AWS Network Firewall in your VPC) - IP level.

ingress_rules.quote: This includes the VPC ID, the VPC subnet IDs, and the VPC security group IDs.
ingress_rules.note: Builds expose no public ports (no public IPv4; CodeBuild ENIs cannot get Elastic IPs). Sandbox access is SSH over SSM Session Manager gated by IAM (ssm:StartSession on the build ARN). VPC builds are governed by your security groups.

guest_firewall.note: Builds run as root; in LINUX_CONTAINER compute NET_ADMIN needs privilegedMode=true (also required for Docker-in-build), EC2-based/reserved fleet compute gives a full VM. Lambda compute has no root, so false there. Not documented explicitly.

secret_proxy.quote: Required if you want to retrieve custom environment variables stored in AWS Secrets Manager.
secret_proxy.note: Secrets from Secrets Manager / Parameter Store are injected as environment variables into the build; no credential-injecting proxy. The managed fleet proxy does network ACLs only.

volume_attach.quote: Information about a file system created by Amazon Elastic File System (EFS).
volume_attach.note: Project fileSystemLocations mount Amazon EFS (NFS 4.1) at a mountPoint in the build container; requires VPC config; Linux only. The one supported type is EFS.

volume_shared.quote: You might want to create your AWS CodeBuild builds on Amazon Elastic File System, a scalable, shared file service for Amazon EC2 instances.
volume_shared.note: EFS is a network file system that concurrent builds (and EC2 instances) can mount read-write at the same time; billed separately by EFS.

isolation.note: Default on-demand builds run as LINUX_CONTAINER (shared-kernel container) on CodeBuild-managed hosts, matching the card's top-level isolation. Reserved-capacity fleets and EC2-based compute types give a dedicated EC2 VM instead, but the modeled default modes are container-based.

image_oci.quote: To use another Docker image, choose Custom image . For Environment type , choose ARM , Linux , Linux GPU , or Windows . ... If you choose Other registry , for External registry URL , enter the name and tag of the Docker image in Docker Hub ... If you choose Amazon ECR , use Amazon ECR repository and Amazon ECR image
image_oci.note: Build projects can start from any custom Docker image in Docker Hub, Amazon ECR, or another OCI-compatible registry (private images supported via Secrets Manager credentials).

nested_virt.quote: By default, Docker daemon is enabled for non-VPC builds. If you would like to use Docker containers for VPC builds ... enable privileged mode. Also, Windows does not support privileged mode.
nested_virt.note: privilegedMode only documents enabling the Docker daemon (Docker-in-Docker) inside the build container; AWS docs never mention /dev/kvm or nested virtualization for CodeBuild build/sandbox environments. Derived: no evidence of KVM passthrough.

browser.quote: AWS CodeBuild is a fully managed continuous integration service that compiles source code, runs tests, and produces software packages that are ready to deploy.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope

anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope

captcha_solving.quote: AWS CodeBuild is a fully managed continuous integration service that compiles source code, runs tests, and produces software packages that are ready to deploy.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope

egress_ip_type.quote: Query external web services that require fixed IP addresses through the Elastic IP address of the NAT gateway or NAT instance associated with your subnet.
egress_ip_type.note: Non-VPC builds egress from CodeBuild-managed AWS IP ranges (ordinary AWS datacenter IPs, no fixed address); VPC-configured builds can obtain a fixed outbound address only via a customer-provisioned NAT gateway/instance Elastic IP, which is still a standard AWS datacenter IP.

ssh.quote: In the SSH Client tab and choose Start sandbox . After the CodeBuild sandbox starts running, follow the console instructions to connect your SSH client with the sandbox.
ssh.note: CodeBuild Sandbox (interactive debug mode) supports connecting an SSH client via SSM Session Manager; plain build runs (Lambda compute, on-demand/reserved builds) do not expose SSH.

own_agent_api.quote: AWS CodeBuild is a fully managed continuous integration service that compiles source code, runs tests, and produces software packages that are ready to deploy.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope

egress_http_rules.quote: Denies outgoing traffic to all destinations by default.
egress_http_rules.note: The managed proxy for reserved-capacity fleets supports orderedProxyRules of type DOMAIN or IP with ALLOW/DENY only; there is no HTTP method/path-level rule. VPC egress control is via security groups/NAT (IP level), also not path-aware.

static_egress_ip.quote: Query external web services that require fixed IP addresses through the Elastic IP address of the NAT gateway or NAT instance associated with your subnet.
static_egress_ip.note: Achieved by running builds inside your own VPC with a NAT gateway/instance that has an Elastic IP - a documented, customer-configured pattern, not a one-click provider feature.

eu_data_residency.quote: Europe (Frankfurt) eu-central-1 ... Europe (Ireland) eu-west-1 ... Europe (London) eu-west-2 ... Europe (Paris) eu-west-3 ... Europe (Stockholm) eu-north-1 ... Europe (Milan) eu-south-1 ... Europe (Spain) eu-south-2 ... Europe (Zurich) eu-central-2
eu_data_residency.note: CodeBuild is available in multiple EU regions; selecting an EU region keeps build execution and artifacts data-resident there.

max_session_h.quote: Build timeout in minutes Each supported Region: 2,160 No Maximum build timeout in minutes
max_session_h.note: 2,160 minutes = 36 hours is the hard (non-adjustable) maximum build/sandbox timeout across all compute types.

persistent_disk.quote: You might want to create your AWS CodeBuild builds on Amazon Elastic File System, a scalable, shared file service for Amazon EC2 instances.
persistent_disk.note: Each build/sandbox's own container/instance disk is ephemeral (nothing checkpointed on stop, per specify-caching-local.html), but CodeBuild first-party supports mounting a persistent Amazon EFS file system (ProjectFileSystemLocation) into the build environment; files written there survive across separate builds/sandboxes since EFS storage is independent of the build lifecycle. Default (no EFS configured) is no persistent disk - ephemeral only; persistence is opt-in via EFS.

volumes.quote: Information about a file system created by Amazon Elastic File System (EFS).
volumes.note: Project fileSystemLocations mount an EFS volume at a mountPoint inside the build container (requires VPC config, Linux only), and that EFS volume can be shared/concurrently mounted by multiple builds/instances (sample-efs.html: 'a scalable, shared file service'). This directly contradicts volumes:false; corrected to true.

snapshot.quote: StartBuild StartBuildBatch StartCommandExecution StartSandbox StartSandboxConnection StopBuild StopBuildBatch StopSandbox
snapshot.note: The complete CodeBuild API action list has no snapshot/checkpoint/image-capture operation for a running build or sandbox; only Start/Stop actions exist. Reserved fleets can boot from a custom AMI, but that configures a fleet ahead of time, it is not a snapshot of a running environment.

pause_resume.note: There is a StopBuild/StopSandbox action but no Resume/Pause action anywhere in the API (API_Operations.html); StopSandbox terminates the session (build/sandbox docs describe builds going RUNNING -> TIMED_OUT/STOPPED, a terminal state) and a new StartSandbox/StartBuild begins a fresh ephemeral environment rather than resuming the stopped one.

fork.quote: StartBuild StartBuildBatch StartCommandExecution StartSandbox StartSandboxConnection StopBuild StopBuildBatch StopSandbox
fork.note: No Fork/Clone/Duplicate operation exists anywhere in the full CodeBuild API action list; each build/sandbox is created fresh from a project definition, not cloned from another instance.

fork_running.quote: StartBuild StartBuildBatch StartCommandExecution StartSandbox StartSandboxConnection StopBuild StopBuildBatch StopSandbox
fork_running.note: Same full action list has no operation to clone a currently-running build/sandbox; no fork capability of any kind is documented.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: StartBuild StartBuildBatch StartCommandExecution StartSandbox StartSandboxConnection StopBuild StopBuildBatch StopSandbox
memory_snapshot_fork.note: No memory/process snapshot-and-fork (CRIU-style) primitive exists in the API or docs; CodeBuild only supports plain Start/Stop of builds and sandboxes.

desktop.quote: In AWS CodeBuild, you can debug a build by using CodeBuild sandbox to run custom commands and troubleshoot your build.
desktop.note: CodeBuild's interactive access is a command-shell/SSH sandbox for build debugging, not a graphical desktop; the product is a CI build service and no VNC/RDP/streamed-desktop feature is documented anywhere in the userguide or console.

computer_use.quote: In AWS CodeBuild, you can debug a build by using CodeBuild sandbox to run custom commands and troubleshoot your build.
computer_use.note: CodeBuild is a CI build/compute service; there is no screenshot+click computer-use API. Its only interactive surface is a command/SSH sandbox for build debugging.

wake_on_request.quote: StartBuild StartBuildBatch StartCommandExecution StartSandbox StartSandboxConnection StopBuild StopBuildBatch StopSandbox
wake_on_request.note: Builds/sandboxes have no 'paused, wakes on request' state - a stopped build/sandbox is terminal; incoming source-repo webhooks (CreateWebhook) trigger a brand-new StartBuild, they don't wake an existing stopped instance.

inbound_https.quote: Make sure that your security groups have no inbound (ingress) traffic allowed to your builds.
inbound_https.note: AWS explicitly recommends builds accept no inbound traffic at all; there is no first-party feature to expose a build/sandbox over inbound HTTPS.

public_ipv4.quote: CodeBuild does not support assigning Elastic IP addresses to the network interfaces that it creates, and auto-assigning a public IP address is not supported by Amazon EC2 for any network interfaces created outside of Amazon EC2 instance launches.
public_ipv4.note: Build/sandbox network interfaces cannot get a public IPv4 address; outbound-only egress via NAT is the documented pattern.

agent_harnesses.quote: A runtime environment image is a container image that runs on top of your chosen compute platform, and includes extra tools that your build might need, such as the AWS CLI.
agent_harnesses.note: CodeBuild's curated runtime images bundle build tooling (AWS CLI, language runtimes, Docker) but AWS does not document any preinstalled/offered coding-agent harness (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, etc.) template.

mcp_server.quote: StartBuild StartBuildBatch StartCommandExecution StartSandbox StartSandboxConnection StopBuild StopBuildBatch StopSandbox
mcp_server.note: No MCP (Model Context Protocol) server or similar agent-driving endpoint is documented anywhere in the CodeBuild API/user guide; the product's own automation surface is the plain REST/SDK API and SSH-via-SSM sandbox.

self_host.quote: You can use the AWS CodeBuild agent to run CodeBuild builds on a local machine.
self_host.note: AWS ships a first-party CodeBuild agent (Docker image, public.ecr.aws/codebuild/local-builds) that runs CodeBuild-compatible builds on your own infrastructure (any machine with Docker), i.e. build execution is self-hostable. The full managed service (fleets, sandbox debug, console) is AWS-only, but the core build-execution capability is not, so false is too strong; corrected to true (build execution) with the managed-service caveat noted.

byoc.quote: Compute refers to the computing engine (the CPU, memory, and operating system) that is managed and maintained by CodeBuild.
byoc.note: All CodeBuild compute (on-demand EC2/Lambda, reserved fleets) runs on AWS-managed infrastructure inside the CodeBuild service account; there is no documented option to deploy the managed control plane into a customer-owned cloud account.

open_source.quote: You can use the AWS CodeBuild agent to run CodeBuild builds on a local machine.
open_source.note: The core CodeBuild service (orchestration API, sandbox, fleets) is AWS proprietary; only the sample base-image Dockerfiles (aws/codebuild-docker-images on GitHub) are open source, and the distributed 'local-builds' agent image itself is a closed AWS binary, not an OSI-licensed release of the product.

live_resize.quote: StartBuild StartBuildBatch StartCommandExecution StartSandbox StartSandboxConnection StopBuild StopBuildBatch StopSandbox
live_resize.note: compute type (vCPU/RAM) is chosen at project/StartBuild time; there is no API to change vCPU/RAM of a running build or sandbox without stopping and starting a new one with a different compute type.

usage_api.quote: You can receive reports that break down your costs by the hour, day, or month, by product or product resource, or by tags that you define yourself.
usage_api.note: granularity: per-tag; cost: yes; AWS Cost and Usage Reports (CUR) and Cost Explorer API allow querying CodeBuild costs filtered by resource tags. Projects/builds are tagged, then Cost Explorer GetCostAndUsage API queries costs for tags matching those builds. Cost data includes money (includes_cost=true). CloudWatch provides live CPU/memory metrics (not billable usage).

persist_scope.quote: You might want to create your AWS CodeBuild builds on Amazon Elastic File System, a scalable, shared file service for Amazon EC2 instances.
persist_scope.note: Only an EFS mount survives a stop; the rest of the filesystem (packages installed elsewhere) resets.

locations_quote: AWS CodeBuild is available in the following regions: us-east-1, us-east-2, us-west-1, us-west-2, ca-central-1, eu-central-1, eu-north-1, eu-south-1, eu-south-2, eu-west-1, eu-west-2, eu-west-3, ap-east-1, ap-south-1, ap-south-2, ap-southeast-1, ap-southeast-2, ap-southeast-3, ap-southeast-4, ap-sout
